cohort_role: post-cohort adoption — the branch inventory is filed because this node is standards-implementing (SPEC §30 implements_standard) and its two-threshold ladder is exactly the shape AUTHORING-STANDARD.md §1 was written for: the corrected 1%/2% ladder replaced art-281's single mis-cited 1% limit, so every branch below was enumerated from the pinned d545 excerpt, never from the kernel.
error_direction_rationale: Every threshold comparison is exact integer cross-multiplication over a declared domain whose degenerate inputs (zero or negative capital, non-centesimal capital, signed or fractional legs, an empty book, an over-cap aggregate) are TYPED REFUSALS rather than approximations, so there is no approximation to have a direction; the direction question does not arise rather than being answered.

branches.branch: The exposure limit applies to the bank's AGGREGATE exposures to Group 2 cryptoassets, not to any single position; the kernel sums the per-asset counted figures into one aggregate before any threshold comparison.
Direct holdings (cash and derivatives) are inside the limit's scope and are supplied as ordinary positions.

Indirect holdings (eg those via investment funds, ETF/ETN, or any legal arrangements designed to provide exposures to cryptoassets) are inside the limit's scope; the holding_type enum names them and every entry counts toward the same aggregate.
An aggregate over an EMPTY book cannot be assessed against the limit; an empty or absent positions array is a typed refusal, never a 0%-clean verdict.
Total exposure to Group 2 cryptoassets should not generally be higher than 1% of Tier 1 — the general-expectation threshold, whose crossing is reported without being a limit breach.
Total exposure to Group 2 cryptoassets must not exceed 2% of Tier 1 — the must-not-exceed limit.
Both comparisons are strict: exactly 1% of Tier 1 is not above the expectation threshold and exactly 2% is not above the limit (v2 and v4 pin both boundaries as conformance vectors).
A percentage-of-Tier-1 threshold is undefined at zero or negative Tier 1 capital; the kernel refuses the input with a typed error instead of emitting a NaN, Infinity, or 0% verdict.

A capital figure not divisible by 100 minor units would make 1% and 2% of it fractional and the excess amount inexact; the kernel refuses rather than round, keeping every threshold comparison in exact integer arithmetic.

Any crossing of the 1% threshold must be communicated immediately to the supervisor: the SUPERVISOR_NOTIFICATION_REQUIRED flag fires in the crossed band (and carries into the breach band, which implies a crossing).
Until compliance with the 1% threshold is restored, only the exposures IN EXCESS of the threshold take the Group 2b capital treatment (the 1250% weight); the remainder keeps its own treatment.
If exposures exceed 2% of Tier 1, ALL Group 2 exposures take the Group 2b treatment: treatment flips to whole_book and the whole aggregate becomes the 2b amount.
Banks must have arrangements in place to ensure compliance with the limit and must rapidly rectify any breach that occurs.

assumption_of_use.value: the bank's compliance arrangements and the remediation actions taken after a finding
assumption_of_use.owner: the bank's risk-management function; this node assesses a point-in-time aggregate and owns no remediation, so a caller treating an assessment output as evidence of rectification misuses it.

branches.branch: 'Until compliance with the 1% limit is restored' makes the excess-only treatment a state that persists over time, not a one-shot verdict.

assumption_of_use.value: the passage of time and the restoration status of the book
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller, who re-runs the assessment as the book and capital change; the kernel sees exactly one snapshot per call and carries no state between calls.

branches.branch: Exposures are measured per separate cryptoasset using the higher of the absolute values of the long and short exposures — never a netted figure; entries naming the same asset have their legs summed first, so the higher-of runs over the asset's totals.
The legs are ABSOLUTE values by definition; a signed leg would invert the higher-of measurement, so a negative or fractional leg is a typed refusal rather than a silently re-signed count.
Derivative exposures must be measured using a delta-equivalent methodology before the higher-of comparison.

assumption_of_use.value: delta-adjusted long_exposure and short_exposure figures per position
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller's valuation function, which supplies legs already delta-adjusted; this node never re-prices a derivative and treats the supplied legs as final.

branches.branch: Tier 1 capital is defined in CAP10.2; the node takes the figure as given rather than recomputing regulatory capital.

assumption_of_use.source: SCO60.119(2), pointing at CAP10.2 for the definition
assumption_of_use.owner: the caller's finance/regulatory-reporting function, which supplies the capital figure; this node owns only the arithmetic done with it.
